issues.detail: Setup leans on Homebrew, `$(brew --prefix)` paths and Claude Code/Codex-specific `mcp add` commands, with no install or registration steps for Windows or for Cursor, Cline and OpenCode, even though the skill lists them as supported.

scenarios.name: claude-code-mcp-setup-home-dir
scenarios.rationale: B gives the brew install, a `claude mcp add` command with `--no-update-check`, the explicit ~/work/monorepo path, a CLAUDE.md line and a healthcheck, which covers the whole rubric; A gives no working setup and only a plan with unverified guesses.

scenarios.name: typescript-agent-search-tool
scenarios.rationale: Response A installs @ff-labs/fff-node, creates a single reused finder through FileFinder.create and checks the ok flag, calls waitForScan, fileSearch and grep with beforeContext and afterContext set to 1, reads relativePath, lineNumber and lineContent from value.items, and calls destroy(), whereas Response B never uses fff and substitutes an rg-based implementation that meets almost none of the rubric.

scenarios.name: neovim-telescope-replacement-lazy
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric: the correct `dmtrKovalenko/fff` repo, the `download_or_build_binary` build, `lazy = false`, `live_grep_under_cursor` with `mode = {"n","x"}`, the `git:modified src/**/*.rs !src/**/mod.rs` token, and `:Lazy clean`. A uses the wrong repo name `fff.nvim`, writes a custom word/selection helper in place of `live_grep_under_cursor()`, gives a prefix-less `*.rs` query and hedges throughout.
